_criterion: Hand-assigned ground truth for the 49 distinct (hearsay source, stored memory) pairs from the paid runs. FLAG if the stored memory asserts the claim with NO marker of uncertainty and NO marker of an external source, where the source carried one. PASS if the memory carries any such marker anywhere in it. ABSTAIN if the extractor stored nothing. AMBIGUOUS where a bare claim line sits beside a sibling line that does carry the attribution, so claim-local and whole-memory reading disagree; these are excluded from headline recall and reported separately rather than resolved by fiat.
_why_this_file_exists: The first live measurement labelled every hearsay-sourced item 'expect flag' regardless of what was actually stored. But the extractor preserved stance roughly two-thirds of the time, so PASS was the correct answer and was being scored as a miss. That put recall at 64% and, worse, optimising against it would have taught the tool to flag correctly-preserved memories. Bad labels are more dangerous than a weak model.
_labelled_by: hand, 2026-08-03, auditable and contestable: every row carries the stored text and a reason
